speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked	the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) how many vehicles have been booked during the past three years for leaving the engine of their stationary vehicles running; (b) what is the duration allowed before the vehicle owner can be penalised; and (c) what is the Ministry doing to raise awareness of this rule to vehicle owners.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Leaving the engine running when the vehicle is stationary, results in fuel wastage and unnecessary environmental pollution.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As part of its outreach programmes, NEA works closely with stakeholders such as the authorised vehicle inspection centres, private and public transport operators and schools to disseminate educational pamphlets and decals so as to raise awareness of the regulation and forewarn motorists not to leave their vehicle engines idling.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To promote greater awareness, NEA has also installed anti-vehicle idling signage at places where vehicles frequently congregate, such as carparks, loading/unloading bays and along the roadside near schools.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Everyone has a part to play in safeguarding our environment and public health.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Members of the public who spot idling vehicles are encouraged to report them to NEA via their hotline or the myENV app.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I am a little surprised to hear that 12,000 had been booked in the last three years.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I would like the Minister to confirm that again.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: In a similar Parliamentary Question (PQ) three years ago, the average number of advisory notes issued was 320 per year.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: But now, the Minister has just replied that 12,000 had been booked.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Why the big jump from 12 to 12,000?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: If the numbers are correct, is there a concern that there are more and more offenders now?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is useful also for people who drive to know that, today, modern technology does not require you to warm up your engine before you drive.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Sometimes, there is this misperception that you have to continue keeping your engine warm so that you can get better fuel efficiency or make the engine last longer.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In reality today, vehicle manufacturers we have consulted say that engines warm up faster to reach the optimal temperature when the vehicle is driven at moderate speeds upon starting.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, I hope people will move away from the old habits.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: With old engines, yes, they need to be warmed up before the vehicles move.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But we need new habits, because engines today do not have to warm up.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Can I ask the Minister what was the quantum of the fine given to these 12,000 offenders?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Should we revise the fines, if the deterrence measures still do not work?
